citazioni: At most security checkpoints in Terminal 1 and at all checkpoints in Terminal 3 , modern CT scanners are in use.

Gates C1, C2, C4, C6
Certain special security checkpoints in Terminal 1
Transfer checkpoints (for connecting passengers)

citazioni: Speed through security: leave your liquids in your bag, and please make sure they are 100ml or less.
Liquids and gels only allowed in containers of up to 100ml in hand luggage
Each item must be 100ml or less. Ensure the volume is clearly visible on the original product label.
No more plastic bags! Our CT security scanners can now scan liquids and electronics inside hand baggage.
eccezioni: The Department for Transport (DfT) has issued the below Directive to UK airports’ using Next Generation Security Checkpoints (NGSC), which includes LCY. From 00:01 on Sunday, 9th June 2024, 100ml restrictions on liquids will temporarily be reintroduced for passengers. However, passengers travelling through London City Airport can still keep everything, including all liquids and large electronics, in their hand luggage when passing through security.
Leave liquids, laptops, tablets and other electronic devices inside hand luggage

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers of 100 ml or less; liquids stay in your bag, no plastic bag (Next Generation Security lanes)
citazioni: Taking liquids and electronics out of your hand luggage at security is no longer necessary thanks to our Next Generation Security lanes.

Liquids are allowed to remain in your hand luggage without the need of a clear plastic bag, with a maximum limit of 100ml per container. There is no need to take them out of your bag when passing through security

Liquids in containers of 100ml or less are permitted to remain in your hand luggage without the need of a clear plastic bag. Exceptions are made for medication (with prescription label) and baby food. For medication and baby food over 100ml, they must be removed from your hand luggage prior to x-ray screening. The term "liquids" includes gels, aerosols (eg. deodorant), pastes (eg. toothpaste), canned goods in sauces (eg. beans or tuna in brine), perfume, makeup (foundation, mascara), e-cigarette cartridges and lighters (only one per person).
eccezioni: Essential medicines may be permitted in large quantities above the 100ml limit, but will be subject to authentication. All medicines should carry the prescription label clearly showing the name of the passenger.
When travelling with a baby, you're allowed to take enough baby food and/or baby milk for the journey, even if that is over the 100ml limit.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers up to 100 ml; liquids stay in your bag (next-generation machines); thermos flasks and metal bottles only if empty
citazioni: On your next visit, you will notice we have recently implemented 'next-generation' security machines within our security search area. This means passengers can now leave liquids and electrical items in their hand baggage during security screening - making the process quicker and more efficient.
Any liquids, aerosols or gels being carried in hand luggage must be in containers of up to 100ml.
eccezioni: Any liquids within double-skinned containers, such as thermos flasks or thermal water bottles, including single layered metal bottles are not able to be scanned and therefore will not be permitted through security. Empty double and single skinned containers are permitted.

Leave liquids up to 2 litres in their hand luggage

All liquids must be in containers that are 100ml or less and placed inside your hand luggage

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers of 100 ml or less, no limit on the number; no plastic bag (CT scanners)
citazioni: Our new CT security scanners offer several key benefits for travellers:
Simplified liquid rules: You can carry an unlimited number of liquids, as long as each container is 100ml or less. These items no longer need to be placed in a separate plastic bag.
eccezioni: We're proud to introduce our new Explosive Detection System (EDS) X-Ray scanners, featuring state-of-the-art Computed Tomography (CT) technology. These next-generation scanners produce high-resolution 3D images of your cabin baggage, improving our ability to detect threats while streamlining the screening process.

citazioni: Further to the UK Government announcement, current requirements for screening liquids and large electricals are unchanged.

Baby feed and drink for the journey may travel in quantities greater than required in the Hand (cabin) Baggage ‘liquids’ Restrictions and there is no need for a clear re-sealable plastic bag.

Passengers can take into the aircraft cabin any liquids bought after passing through the security search area, as these items go through a separate screening process. This includes bottled water, wines and spirits and fragrances and cosmetics of any size.

If you need to, you can take small quantities of liquids through security. These liquids must be in containers no larger than 2,000ml. These liquids can remain within your hand luggage and do not need to be removed for the screening process.
Containers larger than 2,000ml such as drinks bottles (including water), even though it might only contain 2,000ml, are NOT permitted.
eccezioni: Please note: as many airports have not yet introduced this new technology, passengers should check restrictions prior to travel as, they may still be required to carry liquids within a clear plastic bag for the return journey back to Bournemouth Airport.

Essential medicines that you will need during your trip must be checked through security. Again, these liquids must be in containers no larger than 2,000ml and can remain within your hand luggage and do not need to be removed for the screening process.
When travelling with a baby you’re allowed to take enough baby food, baby milk and sterilised water for the journey. In some cases this will be over 2,000ml.

Individual containers of breast milk must hold no more than 2,000ml. Each container will need to be screened at the security point. Airport staff might need to open the containers to screen the liquids.

Passengers should prepare liquids gels and pastes under 100ml in a single, transparent, resealable plastic bag with a total content maximum of 1 litre (approximately 20cm x 20cm). Passengers will need to present these separately at Passenger Screening.

You cannot bring any liquids, lotions, gels or pastes over 100 millilitres on board the aircraft. These items can only be checked in as Hold Baggage. Please give any such items to the security screening staff, who will dispose of them for you.
eccezioni: Passengers travelling with babies and young children are permitted to bring as much baby formula, milk and snacks as is required for the duration of the flight. Please ask one of our security team members for a special tray to put the liquids in as it will be subjected to additional screening as well as going through the x-ray machine.
Essential Prescription Medicines and special dietary requirements including baby foods required for the flight are permitted but these must be presented separately for screening.

eccezioni: Medical and special food products (e.g., baby food) to be consumed during the journey. Authentication may be requested.

eccezioni: Larger quantities are permitted for medical purposes, baby food, or liquids purchased in the duty-free area (with proof).

fonte2.titolo: Antalya Airport (Fraport TAV) – Exceptions to liquid restrictions
citazioni: You may still carry medicines and special dietary requirements, including baby foods, for use during the trip in your hand luggage. You may be asked for proof that they are needed and/or required to taste the contents of each jar or bottle.

All tax-free liquids purchased at the airport duty-free shops located beyond the passport control or on board of the airline are permitted. Liquids purchased at duty-free are sold in a special sealed bag. Do not open it before you are screened - otherwise the contents will be confiscated at the checkpoint.

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers, 1 litre in total, in a transparent bag placed in a tray
citazioni: Liquids: Maximum 100ml per container. Total liquid volume shouldn't exceed 1 litre. Place all liquids in a transparent zipper bag. Remove this bag from your hand luggage and place it in a tray.
eccezioni: Medication in liquid form that you require during your flight is permitted but may need to go through a liquid screening machine if the packaging is larger than 100ml.
Infant formula is permitted provided the infant is travelling with you.

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in one 1-litre bag (about 20 x 20 cm), one bag per passenger
citazioni: If you are carrying any liquids, gels or pastes in your hand luggage, the following restrictions apply:
The liquid must be in a container with a maximum volume of 100ml
Containers must be carried in a single, transparent, re-sealable plastic bag, which holds no more than a litre and measures approximately 20cm x 20cm
The bag must not be knotted or tied at the top
Each passenger can carry only one of these bags
eccezioni: Liquid medicines, baby milk and liquids for special dietary requirements in containers greater than 100ml, but considered necessary for the trip, can be placed in hand luggage but will be subject to a separate verification process
Re-sealable bag of liquids – it will be screened separately from your hand baggage

Please note that liquid restrictions will remain in place at Glasgow Prestwick Airport.
eccezioni: Remember, you can purchase any liquid, aerosol or gel item – including Duty-Free – after security and carry these on board (but check your airline for flights with stopovers).

Baby products required for the duration of the flight are exempt. These include baby milk, sterilised water (that’s in a baby bottle), baby food and wet wipes. Any baby products over 100ml will be screened using enhanced technology.
Essential medication over 100ml will be screened using enhanced technology.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers up to 100 ml, no plastic bag, liquids stay in your bag, no limit on the number

Liquids in your hand luggage do not need to be placed in a plastic bag and do not need to be taken out of your bags prior to screening. There is no specified limit to the number of 100ml liquid containers that may be carried.
eccezioni: Passengers flying from Teesside are advised to carry all non-essential liquids in hold luggage.
aeroporti.titolo_fonte: Teesside International Airport – Preparing for security

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in one 1-litre bag (about 20 x 20 cm), shown at security
citazioni: If you do take liquids in your hand luggage:
Containers must hold no more than 100ml
Containers must be in a single, transparent, resealable plastic bag, which holds no more than a litre and measures approximately 20cm x 20cm
Contents must fit comfortably inside the bag so it can be sealed
The bag must not be knotted or tied at the top
You’re limited to 1 plastic bag per person
You must show the bag at the airport security search area
eccezioni: Liquids in containers larger than 100ml generally cannot go through security even if the container is only part full. There are some exemptions.
You can take liquid containers larger than 100ml through security if they:
Are for essential medical purposes
Are for special dietary requirements
Contain baby food or baby milk
You can also take liquids bought at an airport or on a plane (such as duty free) through security if:
The items are sealed inside a security bag when you buy them
the receipt for the items is sealed in the security bag and visible

contesto.titolo: Hand luggage restrictions at UK airports – Liquids
citazioni: The rules for carrying liquids in your hand luggage depend on the airport.
At most airports, you cannot take liquids in containers larger than 100ml through security. This still applies if the container is only part full.
Some airports may allow you to take liquid in containers that hold up to 2 litres of liquid.

Liquids carried in the aircraft cabin such as aerosols, drinks, toothpaste, cosmetic creams or gels must be carried in a transparent plastic bag - maximum capacity 1 litre - and no container may hold more than 100 ml.

Follow your departure airport's own page.
